name: Small satellite bus
description: A light, cheap frame. It carries one instrument and can't hold a heavy spacecraft.

name: Medium spacecraft bus
description: The workhorse frame for robotic missions. Room for two instruments.

name: Large spacecraft bus
description: A big, strong frame for flagship missions. Three instruments, but heavy.

name: Crew capsule (2 seats)
description: A pressurised capsule for two astronauts on short trips: Earth orbit or the Moon.

name: Deep-space transit habitat (4 crew)
description: A home for four astronauts on a trip lasting more than a year. Needs a lot of power.

name: Small solar array
description: Makes 800 W in full sunlight near Earth. Farther from the Sun it makes much less.

name: Medium solar array
description: Makes 3,000 W near Earth: enough for most robotic spacecraft in the inner Solar System.

name: Giant solar wings
description: Huge wings that make 14,000 W near Earth. At Jupiter, sunlight is only 3.7% as strong, so they make about 520 W there.

name: Crew-rated solar wings
description: Makes 20,000 W near Earth to keep astronauts and their life support running.

name: Habitat solar farm
description: A field of panels making 60,000 W near Earth, about 26,000 W at Mars.

name: Radioisotope generator pack (RTG)
description: Turns heat from decaying plutonium into 470 W, with or without sunlight. Its power slowly fades over decades.

name: Small battery
description: Stores 1,000 Wh to keep things running in a planet's shadow.

name: Medium battery
description: Stores 4,000 Wh. Lasts about ten years.

name: Large battery bank
description: Stores 20,000 Wh: enough for a crewed spacecraft through a long eclipse.

name: Basic flight computer
description: Cheap and light, but it can't fix problems on its own and radiation damages it quickly.

name: Autonomous flight computer
description: Can run the spacecraft on its own when Earth is minutes away by radio.

name: Radiation-hardened computer
description: Built to survive intense radiation for decades. Expensive.

name: Magnetorquers
description: Turns the spacecraft by pushing against Earth's magnetic field. Only works near Earth, and only roughly.

name: Reaction wheels
description: Spinning wheels that turn the spacecraft accurately, anywhere in space.

name: Precision pointing system
description: Star trackers and spare wheels. Steady enough for a space telescope.

name: UHF radio
description: A tiny radio. Fine in Earth orbit, useless far away.

name: S-band antenna
description: Good for Earth orbit and the Moon.

name: X-band high-gain dish
description: A dish antenna that reaches across the Solar System. It must point at Earth.

name: Ka-band large dish
description: Four times the data of X-band at any distance. Heavy and power-hungry.

name: Small thruster pack
description: Simple thrusters for small course corrections.

name: Main engine
description: A strong engine for getting into orbit around another world.

name: Crew service module
description: Engine and big tanks that push a crew capsule into lunar orbit and home again.

name: Deep-space methane stage
description: A big, efficient stage for crewed trips to Mars and back.

name: Nuclear thermal engine (concept)
description: A mission concept: a reactor heats hydrogen to about twice the exhaust speed of chemical engines. Heavy and expensive, but it makes fast trips possible.

name: Spot shielding
description: Thin covers over the most sensitive chips. Halves the dose to the electronics.

name: Titanium radiation vault
description: A titanium box around the electronics, like the vault that protects Juno at Jupiter.

name: Storm shelter (water walls)
description: A small room lined with water tanks where the crew hide during solar storms.

name: Polyethylene hull lining
description: Hydrogen-rich plastic all around the crew. Heavy, but it cuts the everyday cosmic-ray dose.

name: Insulation blankets
description: Gold-coloured blankets that keep temperatures steady near Earth.

name: Heaters and insulation
description: Electric heaters that keep the spacecraft warm far from the Sun.

name: Sunshield
description: A big shade that keeps a telescope cold and dark, so it can see faint objects.

name: Stored supplies only
description: Carry all the water, air and food. Simple, but heavy on long trips.

name: Water and air recycler
description: Recovers 60% of the water and oxygen, so you carry far less.

name: Closed-loop life support
description: Recovers 85% of the water and oxygen. Heavy and power-hungry, but saves tonnes on long trips.

name: Exercise equipment
description: Treadmill and resistance machines. Slows bone and muscle loss in weightlessness.

name: Spinning habitat arm
description: Spins the crew quarters on an arm to make artificial gravity. A longer arm spins slower and feels more comfortable.

name: Earth-orbit heat shield
description: Survives re-entry from Earth orbit (about 7.8 km/s).

name: Lunar-return heat shield
description: Survives the faster re-entry when coming home from the Moon (about 11 km/s).

name: Mars-return heat shield
description: Survives the fastest re-entries, coming home from Mars (about 12.5 km/s).
